sentences.text: Three more signals, and the first one could save your life.

When vessels in sight are approaching each other, and one doesn’t understand the other’s intentions, or doubts she’s doing enough to avoid a collision, she immediately sounds at least five short, rapid blasts.
It can be backed up with at least five short, rapid flashes of a light.
So when should you use it?
It doesn’t mean you’re angry, and it doesn’t mean you’re right.
It means: I don’t understand what you’re doing.
You met it in lesson four: a vessel nearing a bend, or a place where other vessels may be hidden, sounds one prolonged blast, and any vessel around the bend answers with one prolonged blast.
Under the Inland rules, one prolonged blast has a second use: a power-driven vessel leaving a dock or berth sounds it.
If a ship has whistles more than one hundred meters apart, she uses only one of them for maneuvering signals.
